entries.0c0afdc26bdbdba1: This business makes products that allow patients to measure their own health or administer drugs at home or elsewhere. It handles blood glucose monitoring systems that measure blood sugar levels, needles for pen-type injectors used to inject insulin, insulin pumps, electronic blood pressure monitors and electronic thermometers, among others. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥20,761 million, down 2.8% year on year.
entries.14047c2d46458d27: This business makes medical supplies used in hospitals and at home, and products for pharmaceutical companies. It ranges from products used daily in hospitals, such as syringes, infusion pumps, infusion sets and infusion solutions, to products used by patients themselves, such as blood glucose monitoring systems and electronic thermometers, and contract manufacturing that fills syringes with drugs. By product group, it is divided into three subsegments: "Hospital Care Solutions," "Life Care Solutions" and "Pharmaceutical Solutions." Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥216,138 million, up 2.3% year on year. In Japan, sales rose 0.4% as the Pharmaceutical Solutions business grew, although affected by the termination of some businesses; overseas, sales rose 7.2% on increases in North America and Europe.
entries.14139d5ed670ee38: This business supports pharmaceutical companies in making medicines. In addition to contract manufacturing of prefilled syringe preparations, in which drugs are filled into syringes in advance, it handles products for pharmaceutical companies, such as syringes for filling drugs and injection needles packaged with medicines. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥49,260 million, up 10.4% year on year, the largest increase within the Medical Care Solutions Company. The company cites this business as one that supported revenue growth in Japan.
entries.1dfa5bbc21ad9031: Aspiration catheters and removal devices for treating ischemic stroke
entries.227179e008c92486: This business manufactures medical devices to treat diseases of the heart, blood vessels, and blood vessels in the brain. It handles guidewires and catheters inserted into blood vessels, balloons and stents that widen blood vessels, artificial lungs and heart-lung machines used in heart surgery, and artificial blood vessels and stent grafts that replace damaged blood vessels. It is divided into four sub-segments by product group: "Interventional Systems," "Neuro," "Cardiovascular," and "Aortic." Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥676,421 million, the largest business of the company's total revenue of ¥1,131,877 million. Compared with the previous year, it rose 8.3%; overseas, all businesses grew, rising 8.6%, and in Japan, the Interventional Systems and Neuro businesses performed well, rising 5.9%.

entries.3b2b361783aed4a7: A Tokyo-based medical device manufacturer that sells equipment used in medical settings, such as catheters, blood bags, syringes and infusion pumps, around the world.
entries.4303eb421b041145: This business makes products that deliver drugs and infusion fluids into patients' bodies in hospitals. It handles syringes, infusion pumps and syringe pumps that deliver fixed amounts accurately, infusion sets, infusion solutions, peritoneal dialysis solutions, analgesics, and materials that prevent adhesions after surgery, among others. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥146,116 million, up 0.6% year on year.

entries.73c8c7f0f307f5db: This business makes devices for treating diseases of large blood vessels such as the aorta. It handles artificial blood vessels that replace damaged vessels, and stent grafts that reinforce vessels from the inside. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥55,993 million, up 4.6% year on year.

entries.8e78ab18f4556798: This business makes equipment for collecting, separating and processing blood. Besides blood bags used for blood donation and transfusion, component collection systems that extract only components such as platelets and plasma from blood, centrifugal devices that separate blood components by centrifugal force, systems that automatically make blood into preparations, and systems that reduce pathogens in blood, it also handles systems for expanding cells and systems for collecting source plasma. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥231,037 million, up 15.4% year on year, the largest increase among the three existing businesses. Overseas, Global Blood Solutions performed well, up 15.5%, as the plasma innovation business expanded in North America; in Japan, sales rose 13.2% as blood collection-related products increased. No sub-segments have been established.

entries.b8749c5bc6112d2e: This business makes devices that take over the functions of the heart and lungs during heart surgery. It handles artificial lungs that supply oxygen to the blood, and heart-lung machines that keep blood flowing through the body. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥70,020 million, up 4.0% year on year.

entries.d4d817c7baa98c4f: This business makes equipment for preserving organs (organ preservation devices). On October 29, 2025, it acquired all shares of Organox, Ltd. and made it a wholly owned subsidiary, and as a result it was newly added as a reportable segment from the fiscal year ended March 2026. Only results from the acquisition date onward are consolidated, and revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥7,985 million. The company explains this as the result of business expansion centered on the North American market.
entries.d9f35a6bd8705ad6: This business makes devices for treating diseases of the blood vessels in the brain. It handles coils and stents that block cerebral aneurysms from the inside, sac-type embolization devices, and aspiration catheters and removal devices that take blood clots out of vessels blocked by cerebral infarction. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥106,902 million, up 10.0% year on year. The company explains that sales of this business were also strong in Japan.

entries.f3b1493d87bc1963: This business makes devices for treating patients by passing thin tubes through blood vessels without making large incisions in the body. It handles guidewires and catheters that travel through blood vessels, introducer sheaths that serve as the entry point for inserting and removing catheters, devices that stop bleeding at puncture sites in arteries at the base of the leg, balloon catheters and stents that widen blood vessels, and catheters that use ultrasound to view the inside of blood vessels, among others. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥443,505 million, the largest within the Cardiovascular Company, up 9.2% year on year.
